tagline: Along the crest of two Ouachita ridges, from Talihina to Mena.
intro: Out of Talihina, a railroad town whose Choctaw name means iron road, Highway 1 climbs onto Winding Stair Mountain and keeps to the crest for 54 miles, along Winding Stair and then Rich Mountain, over the Arkansas line as Highway 88 and down into Mena. There are 22 vista pull-outs on the way, Castle Rock and Sugarloaf among them, and grades of 13 percent.

Much of the forest on these ridgetops is stunted, worth too little to cut, so it was never logged. The road opened in 1969, and Lucy Baines Johnson, Lyndon Johnson's daughter, dedicated it the next June.
season: Autumn. TravelOK calls the drive particularly beautiful in the fall, and ARDOT notes its fall foliage.

moments.title: Winding Stair Mountains
moments.text: In territorial days this ridge was the boundary between Sugar Loaf County and Wade County in the Choctaw Nation, and its higher peaks reach about 2,400 feet.

moments.title: Queen Wilhelmina State Park
moments.text: A railroad with Dutch investors opened a lodge on Rich Mountain in 1898 and named it for a queen not yet crowned. The lodge there now is the third.

moments.title: Mena
moments.text: Arthur Stilwell founded the town in 1896 while building that railroad and named it for his Dutch financier's wife, whom her husband called Mena.
